races.name: Racing TV Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Rialannah
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who needs strong pace and may find this tactical setup challenging, but Lucy Wadham stable in decent form recently
runners_data.comment: Ran big race when fifth on recent stable debut and this longer trip will suit; shortlisted
runners_data.spotlight: 0-15 over hurdles but posted some good efforts for the Joel Parkinson-Sue Smith stable last term and ran a big race when fifth on recent seasonal/stable debut at Uttoxeter (2m4f, good to soft); will be suited by this move back up in trip; one to consider.

runners_data.name: Tropical Speed
runners_data.note: Has fitness concerns after 137-day break but won last time out making all, suggesting versatility in running style
runners_data.comment: Off since making all at Lingfield in November but this faster ground may suit even better
runners_data.spotlight: Consistent and progressive 7yo who made all to score by 6l at Lingfield (2m7f, good to soft) on latest outing; has fitness to prove after 137-day break but could plausibly be seen to even better effect on the forecast faster ground here.

runners_data.name: Breezethroughlife
runners_data.note: Prominent racer perfectly positioned to track The Wise Traveller and has winning course form plus Neil King's 50% strike rate
runners_data.comment: Second on handicap debut; struggled on next two outings; had wind op last month
runners_data.spotlight: Won small-field course maiden (2m4f, good) on stable debut in October and was creditable second on handicap debut at Doncaster (3m, good to soft) in December; big player if judged on those exploits but struggled on last two outings, and much depends on the success of last month's wind op.

runners_data.name: Ilitch
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who bled last time but showed class when second at Doncaster, needs strong gallop to be effective
runners_data.comment: Flopped badly last time (bled); contender if judged on previous Doncaster second
runners_data.spotlight: Flopped badly when favourite at Warwick last month (bled from the nose) but was one of two to pull clear of the others when second at Doncaster (3m, soft) in January and will be suited by the forecast faster ground here; can feature if back on song.

runners_data.name: Mahon Falls
runners_data.note: Prominent runner stepping up from Irish maidens but Shane Quinlan's 3lb claim helps, only 15 days since last run
runners_data.comment: Didn't achieve much when remote third of four on recent stable debut; handicap debut today
runners_data.spotlight: Placed in three Irish maiden hurdles (2m1f-2m5f) for Willie Mullins in the autumn but probably didn't achieve much when remote third of four on stable debut a fortnight ago (2m3f); up in trip for this handicap debut; needs that recent outing to have brought her on.

runners_data.name: Alan Bresil
runners_data.note: Hold-up type who has been running consistently without winning, 7lb claimer Harry Reed takes over riding duties
runners_data.comment: 0-6 over hurdles but not beaten that far at Ascot recently and this race looks easier
runners_data.spotlight: 0-6 over hurdles but wasn't beaten that far when fifth of eight at Ascot (2m7f, good) a fortnight ago and this race looks less competitive; could have a say.

runners_data.name: The Wise Traveller
runners_data.note: Confirmed front runner whose recent form is poor but has significant weight advantage and quick turnaround after pulling up
runners_data.comment: Generally disappointing since Plumpton win in September; pulled up there last week
runners_data.spotlight: Made all to cause 25-1 surprise at Plumpton (3m1f, good) in September, after a break, but generally disappointing since; pulled up when back at Plumpton a week ago, and can't be supported with much confidence here.

runners_data.name: Raby Mere
runners_data.note: Prominent racer returning to form with cheekpieces fitted, has good recent course winner but 4lb rise to contend with
runners_data.comment: Back in prime form at Southwell last week and also has a course win on his CV; respected
runners_data.spotlight: Returned to peak form in refitted cheekpieces at Southwell (3m, good) three weeks ago, his third start for Caroline Fryer; recent 4lb rise does not look excessive and he also has a course win on his CV; respected.

races.paceDynamic: The Wise Traveller will look to make all the running from the front, with Breezethroughlife and Mahon Falls likely tracking prominently in second and third. Behind them, the hold-up horses Rialannah, Tropical Speed, and Ilitch will settle towards the rear, while Alan Bresil and Raby Mere occupy mid-division berths. With only one confirmed front-runner in an 8-runner field over 2m7½f, The Wise Traveller can dictate a steady gallop without early pressure. This tactical setup strongly favours the prominent racers and those with tactical speed, as they can position close enough to strike when the pace inevitably quickens, while pure hold-up horses may find themselves with too much ground to make up.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Steady Pace Suits Prominents
scenarios.trigger: If The Wise Traveller sets an uncontested lead and the pace stays steady until the home turn.
scenarios.body: Breezethroughlife and Mahon Falls can track the leader comfortably before challenging with their superior class and fitness. The hold-up horses struggle to close the gap when the race develops into a tactical affair.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Strong Gallop Tests Stamina
scenarios.trigger: If the pace becomes genuine early with Raby Mere or Breezethroughlife pressing The Wise Traveller.
scenarios.body: The stronger gallop plays to the stamina strengths of Ilitch and Tropical Speed who can pick up the pieces late. Rialannah's proven staying power also comes into play over this extended trip.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If The Wise Traveller bounces back to his Plumpton winning form and maintains a strong gallop throughout.
scenarios.body: Despite his recent poor efforts, The Wise Traveller's class rating of 113 TS suggests he has the ability to wire the field. His 18lb weight advantage over the main contenders becomes crucial in the closing stages.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Collapse Creates Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If The Wise Traveller stops quickly or falls, leaving no clear pace angle in the race.
scenarios.body: The race becomes a muddling affair where horses with tactical speed like Alan Bresil and Raby Mere can position prominently. Late-running types benefit from the slower overall time but need to be closer than usual.

watchPoints.text: If The Wise Traveller shows early signs of distress or reluctance, as he pulled up just seven days ago at Plumpton
Watch for Tropical Speed's fitness after 137 days off, particularly how he handles the early pace having won last time making all
Breezethroughlife's positioning in the first half-mile will be crucial as he needs to track close enough to The Wise Traveller without getting involved in early pace battles
Monitor how aggressively Raby Mere and Mahon Falls position themselves, as both have shown prominent tendencies that could pressure the leader
Keep an eye on Ilitch for any signs of bleeding given his last-start issue, which could affect his ability to finish strongly

races.name: Weatherbys nhstallions.co.uk Mares' Handicap Chase (Queen Boudicca Mares' Chase Series Qualifier)

runners_data.name: Moviddy
runners_data.note: Hold-up style with superior RPR of 103 but 21-day break since last run creates slight fitness question despite her class edge.
runners_data.comment: Regressive and inconsistent now but ran well in valuable series final here in January
runners_data.spotlight: Arrested her decline when placed in valuable final of this mares' series here (2m5f, good to soft; refitted cheekpieces) in January; two lesser efforts have followed and she's unreliable nowadays but she could be too good for this field if perked up by a change of headgear.

runners_data.name: Gilbertina
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with tactical advantage as lone pace-setter, benefits from Tom Midgley's 3lb claim reducing effective weight to 164lbs.
runners_data.comment: Below par this month but was close third over 2m4f two runs ago; tries a new trip here
runners_data.spotlight: Slightly disappointing at Southwell 12 days ago and now 0-6 over fences but her close third at Newcastle (2m4f, good to soft) was a pretty good effort and she has possibilities here if stamina holds out on first venture beyond about 2m5f.

runners_data.name: Fortunefavorsdbold
runners_data.note: Prominent style should see her track the leader Gilbertina, but poor recent form at Southwell raises questions about current wellbeing.
runners_data.comment: Placed on four of her five outings this season and features prominently in calculations
runners_data.spotlight: Suffered early mishap three starts ago but placed on other four outings this season, most recently when second ay Exeter (3m, good) three weeks ago; ran poorly on only previous visit to Fakenham and would appeal more on ground slower than good but still features prominently in calculations.

runners_data.name: Annie Nail
runners_data.note: Hold-up merchant with excellent course record but inconsistent form makes her unreliable despite 7-day quick turnaround.
runners_data.comment: Not very consistent but won over hurdles off today's mark a week ago
runners_data.spotlight: Won over fences here (2m5f, good) last spring and doubled her course tally in modest handicap hurdle (2m7f, good) a week ago; far too inconsistent to rely upon heavily but reverts to chasing on a good mark and has obvious claims if in the right mood again.

runners_data.name: Ballygelly
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner who won this exact race last year on good ground but 28-day absence and erratic form pattern create concerns.
runners_data.comment: Well beaten last month, after a break, but ran well over C&D twice last year
runners_data.spotlight: Beat 1-9 favourite when winning two-runner edition of this race a year ago (good ground) and was in front before last-fence unseat over C&D (good to soft) in October; returned from break with low-key run last month but remains lightly raced for her age, and her course form is a selling point.

races.paceDynamic: Gilbertina is the only confirmed front runner in this small field and should get an uncontested lead with Fortunefavorsdbold likely to track her in second. The three hold-up horses (Moviddy, Annie Nail, Ballygelly) will sit back and rely on late challenges over the final half-mile. With no pace pressure early, Gilbertina can dictate terms and potentially steal a march, but the galloping nature of Fakenham's 3m trip typically sees races develop into proper staying tests. This setup favours prominent runners who can position close enough to the pace to strike when it matters, as the hold-up brigade may find too much ground to make up if Gilbertina gets first run.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Front Runner Steals It
scenarios.trigger: If Gilbertina maintains a steady gallop and quickens before the hold-up horses can respond...
scenarios.body: She can exploit her tactical advantage by getting first run on the turn for home while the closers are still organizing their challenges. Tom Midgley's 3-claim reduces her burden to an effective 164lbs, making her harder to peg back.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Surge Succeeds
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace allows the hold-up horses to get into contention turning for home...
scenarios.body: Moviddy's superior class (OR 97, RPR 103) can tell in a driving finish, especially given her previous course success. The 21-day break since her last run could have her primed for improvement.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Course Specialist Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Annie Nail reproduces her course-winning form from last spring...
scenarios.body: Her dual course success (over fences and hurdles) gives her a significant edge, and the 7-day turnaround suggests connections are confident. At just 145lbs, she receives a huge weight advantage over the principals.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Repeat Winner Returns
scenarios.trigger: If Ballygelly can replicate her victory in this exact race twelve months ago...
scenarios.body: Her proven course and distance credentials are undeniable, but the 28-day layoff and inconsistent form create doubts. The good ground conditions match her previous winning conditions perfectly.

watchPoints.text: Watch if Gilbertina gets an easy lead early - she could steal a decisive advantage before the closers get organized.
Monitor Annie Nail's position turning for home given her dual course wins and significant weight advantage at just 145lbs.
Check if Moviddy travels strongly in the back half - her superior RPR of 103 could prove decisive in a driving finish.
Observe Fortunefavorsdbold's jumping rhythm early as any mistakes could end her chances of tracking the pace effectively.
Watch Ballygelly for signs of her best form returning given her exact race victory here twelve months ago.

races.name: Woodfordes Mares' Novices' Limited Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Honey I'm Good
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with 7lb claim who shaped better than finishing position suggests last time and has workable handicap mark
runners_data.comment: Well handicapped on old form and shaped quite well in February, after a long layoff
runners_data.spotlight: Well handicapped on 2024 hurdle/chase form and shaped with a fair but more promise than eventual 40l defeat might suggest at Sedgefield (3m3f, good to soft) in February, after a long absence; ought to be better suited by the forecast faster ground here; interesting.

runners_data.name: Dartmouth Rose
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer coming off career-best win in first-time cheekpieces but faces 7lb rise which asks plenty at this level
runners_data.comment: Career-best form when scoring in new cheekpieces last month; this C&D also suits
runners_data.spotlight: Probably showed career-best form when scoring in first-time cheekpieces at Southwell (2m4f, good) last month; 7lb rise asks quite a lot of her but this C&D also suits and the headgear may prompt further improvement; big player.

runners_data.name: Silver Gale
runners_data.note: Needs strong pace from rear having fared much better on handicap debut over longer trip, warning that she fades in finish
runners_data.comment: Improved form when upped to 3m2f for recent handicap debut, finishing third
runners_data.spotlight: Well beaten at triple-digit odds in her three qualifying races (2m-2m3f) but fared much better when third of seven on recent handicap debut at Warwick (3m2f, good); that was a modest contest but she remains lightly raced.

runners_data.name: Natus Vincere
runners_data.note: Natural front-runner with class edge who can dictate terms unopposed, but 29 days since last run may need the outing

races.paceDynamic: Natus Vincere will take this field along from the front with no natural pace rivals, setting a controlled gallop over this staying trip. Honey I'm Good may track in second from her prominent position, while Dartmouth Rose and Silver Gale will be held up in the rear of this small field. With Natus Vincere unopposed for the lead, he can dictate fractions and kick when ready, creating a tactical race where the front-runner holds all the cards. This race shape strongly favours the leader and any horse with tactical speed to respond to his move.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Front Runner Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If Natus Vincere gets an uncontested lead and kicks clear approaching the last
scenarios.body: With no pace pressure, he can time his effort perfectly and use his class advantage to pull clear late. The hold-up horses will struggle to make up ground against a controlled gallop.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Honey I'm Good travels smoothly tracking Natus Vincere and outfinishes him
scenarios.body: Her handicap mark looks workable based on 2024 form and she can use her prominent style to stay close enough to strike. Eleanor Williams' 7lb claim becomes crucial in a tight finish.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Late Surge
scenarios.trigger: If the pace becomes genuinely strong and Dartmouth Rose gets a perfect run from the rear
scenarios.body: Her recent Southwell win showed career-best form and Jack Quinlan can time a late challenge if the leaders weaken. The 7lb rise remains a concern but class may tell.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Benefits Closer
scenarios.trigger: If Natus Vincere goes too fast early trying to kill off the race
scenarios.body: Silver Gale could benefit from a strongly-run race despite her poor qualifying form, as her third at Warwick over 3m2f suggests she needs a test of stamina. Gavin Sheehan knows how to produce a late run.

watchPoints.text: Natus Vincere if he gets loose on the front end - no natural pace rival to apply pressure until it's too late
Honey I'm Good's jumping under pressure - needs to travel smoothly to use her prominent position effectively
Silver Gale's early position - if held too far back she may not get home despite needing a strong pace
Dartmouth Rose without cheekpieces - won last time in first-time headgear so removal could blunt effectiveness
The pace through the middle section - if Natus Vincere goes too steady the hold-up horses get a better chance

races.name: Woodfordes Supports Dereham Meeting Point Handicap Chase

runners_data.name: Slaney Opera
runners_data.note: Former pointer who has adapted well to handicaps under rules, with Harry Reed's 5lb claim valuable at this extended trip
runners_data.comment: Won at Sedgefield in January and ran well in defeat last month; now with new stable
runners_data.spotlight: Former pointer/hunter chaser who won Sedgefield handicap (3m2f, good to soft) for Ruth Jefferson in January and signed off for her with clear second at Wetherby (3m, good) last month; upped in trip and fitted with cheekpieces for this stable debut; likely contender.

runners_data.name: Esperti
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up performer whose dual wins show he thrives in small fields where he can time his challenge

runners_data.name: Prince Cleni
runners_data.note: Natural front runner who will enjoy the uncontested lead but may struggle to repel closers off steady fractions

runners_data.name: Blackacre
runners_data.note: Major fitness concern after 175-day absence, though his Newton Abbot wins prove his effectiveness at this distance
runners_data.comment: Dual winner last summer; absent since the autumn but resumes on a workable mark
runners_data.spotlight: Won twice in a visor at Newton Abbot (3m2f, good/good to soft) last summer; untested beyond that trip and absent since respectable second of three in the autumn (without headgear, as today) but current mark is workable if he's fully tuned up.

races.paceDynamic: Prince Cleni will dictate from the front in this small field, with his natural front-running style facing no pressure from three confirmed hold-up horses. The sustainable pace will allow all four to stay in touch through the early stages, but the lack of pace pressure means the race will develop into a tactical affair. The moderate gallop will suit horses with a strong finishing kick who can quicken off the steady tempo. This race shape clearly favours hold-up horses with tactical speed who can exploit the lack of early pace.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Tactical Hold-Up Battle
scenarios.trigger: If Prince Cleni sets uncontested fractions and the field remains bunched turning in
scenarios.body: The steady pace allows all three closers to arrive with chances, favouring those with the best finishing kick and race fitness. Esperti and Slaney Opera can unleash their strongest weapons in the final half-mile.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Kicks Clear
scenarios.trigger: If Prince Cleni quickens approaching two out and gets first run on his rivals
scenarios.body: The leader exploits his positional advantage when the closers are still getting organized, building a decisive advantage. His stamina reserves prove crucial over this extended trip.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Blackacre Returns Fresh
scenarios.trigger: If Blackacre's 175-day break has recharged his batteries and he produces his Newton Abbot form
scenarios.body: The longest-absent runner surprises with a bold late challenge, his freshness compensating for lack of recent race practice. His proven staying ability at this trip becomes the decisive factor.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses Completely
scenarios.trigger: If Prince Cleni goes too slowly and the race becomes a crawling sprint finish
scenarios.body: The lack of genuine pace turns this into a messy scramble where positioning and luck matter more than ability. The horse who gets the clearest run in the final furlong prevails.

watchPoints.text: Prince Cleni's early fractions - if he goes too fast early he'll compromise his stamina reserves for the finish
Blackacre's jumping fluency after his long layoff - any rustiness will end his chances in this small field
How aggressively Sean Bowen positions Esperti - his tactical placement will determine if he can unleash his finishing kick
Slaney Opera's settling ability behind the steady pace - if he pulls hard he'll negate his stamina advantage
The pace through the middle section - if it remains pedestrian, the finish will be all about who produces the strongest surge

races.name: Weatherbys Design & Print Maiden Hurdle (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Jamada
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with strong recent form who finished ahead of Sense Of Reason last time and should relish the likely tactical scenario.

runners_data.name: Crackalackin
runners_data.note: Prominent runner making hurdling debut off a 34-day break, but his flat form suggests he has the pace to make all if adapting quickly.
runners_data.comment: Fair Flat racer who has possibilities at this level if he takes to hurdling
runners_data.spotlight: Fair Flat racer who won on Polytrack in the autumn (1m4f; RPR 78); ran poorly on latest outing five weeks ago but can be very competitive at this level if he takes to hurdling at the first attempt; usual cheekpieces replace blinkers.

runners_data.name: Sense Of Reason
runners_data.note: Another hold-up performer who needs the race to develop into a test of stamina rather than speed from his patient position.
runners_data.comment: Safely held on handicap debut but first two hurdles runs were encouraging
runners_data.spotlight: Won on the AW last summer (1m2f) and launched hurdling career with two encouraging fourths, latterly when just over 2l behind Jamada in 18-runner Lingfield maiden (2m, soft) in January; safely held on subsequent handicap debut but still considered here, with the switch to better ground a possible source of improvement.

runners_data.name: Somkiyr
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with modest form whose trainer is out of form, but the 28-day gap since his last run could have him sharper.

races.paceDynamic: Crackalackin will set the pace from the front with minimal pressure in this small field, likely accompanied by Somkiyr in the early stages before that one drops away. The sustainable tempo will suit those who can travel well behind the leader, with Jamada and Sense Of Reason both possessing the class to pick up the pieces. With only four runners and one clear pace-setter, this sets up perfectly for hold-up horses who can time their challenge, as the lack of early pace pressure means Crackalackin may have enough left to be caught by superior class late on.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Class Tells Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace stays steady and the race becomes a sprint from the last
scenarios.body: Jamada and Sense Of Reason can utilize their superior ratings to reel in Crackalackin's honest gallop. The hold-up pair have the tactical speed to capitalize when the leader weakens approaching the final flight.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Wire-To-Wire Special
scenarios.trigger: If Crackalackin adapts immediately to hurdling and maintains his flat speed
scenarios.body: His uncontested lead could prove decisive if he jumps cleanly and finds the switch from polytrack to turf hurdles seamless. The lack of early pace pressure preserves his stamina for a sustained kick.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Somkiyr Gate-Crashes
scenarios.trigger: If the recent run has sharpened Somkiyr beyond his modest ratings suggest
scenarios.body: He could press Crackalackin early then find extra reserves when the favorites make their moves. His prominent style keeps him in touch when the pace quickens.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Drama
scenarios.trigger: If all runners wait too long and Crackalackin gets an easy lead throughout
scenarios.body: The lack of pressure could see him steal a march that proves unpeggable despite his modest hurdling debut. Even classy hold-up horses need something to aim at.

watchPoints.text: Watch Crackalackin's jumping on hurdling debut - any mistakes could hand the race to the hold-up pair
Monitor if Jamada gets too far back in a slowly-run race as he may need the tempo to lift
Check if Somkiyr can press the pace early enough to set up the race for the closers
Watch for Tom Cannon being too patient on Sense Of Reason in a race that may lack genuine pace
Observe if the small field creates tactical complications for the hold-up horses

races.name: Sandcliff Cromer "Grassroots" Maiden Hunters' Chase (For The Turner Trophy)

runners_data.name: On Lovers Walk
runners_data.note: Will lead throughout but 242 days off and new stable connections are concerns despite recent point win
runners_data.comment: Fair under rules in Ireland; comfortably won a point on stable debut a week ago
runners_data.spotlight: Showed some fair form under rules when based in Ireland and comfortably won minor point at Paxford (2m4f, good) for new stable a week ago; not sure to be suited by this move back up in trip but still commands respect; sports refitted tongue-tie and first-time cheekpieces.

runners_data.name: Mister Splash
runners_data.note: Hold up horse with excellent recent point form at this track but amateur rider against conditionals
runners_data.comment: 4-14 in points, including course win last month; likely contender
runners_data.spotlight: Not seen under rules since 2022 but 4-14 in points in the meantime, including success at this track (3m, good) last month and in Higham match race ten days ago; likely contender.

runners_data.name: Chapelier
runners_data.note: Veteran hold up runner but woeful recent record and 14-year-old legs questionable over 3m
runners_data.comment: Teenager who has very uninspiring record in points in recent years
runners_data.spotlight: Teenager who is 0-18 under rules, and has very uninspiring record in points in recent years; remote when third of four on recent seasonal debut at Higham; difficult to enthuse over.

runners_data.name: Royal Cave
runners_data.note: Hold up style with surprise recent point win but inconsistent Irish form raises stamina doubts
runners_data.comment: Surprise winner of a point last month but safely held since; chase debut today
runners_data.spotlight: Out of form over hurdles/on the Flat in Ireland last year; caused 16-1 surprise in point at Hutton Rudby (3m, soft) last month, her third start for this stable, but was safely held on next outing; not easy to predict on chase debut.

races.paceDynamic: On Lovers Walk will likely lead from the start given their prominent style and lack of other natural front runners in this small field. With Mister Splash, Chapelier and Royal Cave all holding up runners, On Lovers Walk should get an easy time in front and dictate terms throughout the 3m trip. The pace will be sustainable rather than searching, as no horse will apply early pressure to the leader. This race shape strongly favours the early leader and prominent runners, as the hold up horses will struggle to close from off the pace against a horse that's had such an easy lead.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Lovers Walk controls
scenarios.trigger: If On Lovers Walk gets the expected easy lead and maintains stamina
scenarios.body: The leader dictates a steady gallop and kicks clear approaching the last fence when the hold up horses are still gathering momentum. Miss Micklewright can time her effort perfectly from the front.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Point experience tells
scenarios.trigger: If Mister Splash's recent point form translates under rules
scenarios.body: The experienced pointer closes strongly in the final half mile, using superior fitness from recent Fakenham and Higham wins. Barlow's 3lb claim becomes crucial in a tight finish.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Cave springs surprise
scenarios.trigger: If Royal Cave reproduces her shock Hutton Rudby point win
scenarios.body: The 7-year-old stays on best of all in the final furlong, benefiting from the 7lb weight allowance and fresher legs than the older horses. Her recent winning form gives confidence.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace collapses completely
scenarios.trigger: If On Lovers Walk stops quickly after a long absence
scenarios.body: The race becomes a crawl and turns into a sprint finish where any of the hold up horses can prevail. Chapelier's veteran experience in tactical affairs could prove decisive despite poor recent form.

watchPoints.text: On Lovers Walk could stop quickly in the straight after 242 days off the track
Mister Splash may struggle to get competitive position from rear with inexperienced amateur jockey
Royal Cave's 7lb weight advantage could prove significant if race becomes tactical
Chapelier looks outclassed but veteran experience in small fields can never be dismissed
Ground conditions remain consistent Good throughout the card favouring all runners equally
